investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent evals (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod the eval runner attempted to schedule was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence of a passing run exists in history, and zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were returned, confirming the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource capacity on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) indicates that no schedulable node exists for a new peer-pod VM. Because the pod never started, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completed, leaving all four required evidence fields unpopulated and causing the expected-output contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256) to fail entirely. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' and '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' across 0/6 nodes, with preemption also unavailable.
failed-check.timing: check failed at latencyMs=127112, well before the outageLatencyMs threshold of 360000, meaning the pod was stuck unscheduled for 120s before the eval timed out.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the agent process never starting.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error, pod stuck for 144s, zero evidence keys returned.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod stuck for 144s, zero evidence keys returned.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; if the pod cannot be scheduled this call never resolves successfully, so no evidence is written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never starts.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:179-187: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are both marked required=true; degradedAfterFailures=1 means the feature is in a degraded state after this single run.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource quota exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: existing peer-pod VMs from prior runs or other workloads have consumed all available slots, leaving no capacity for new agent pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity/selector rules, meaning only 2 nodes are ever eligible. If those 2 nodes have even a small vm quota, any concurrent load exhausts it. Supported by '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' in failed-check.message.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie peer-pod VMs from previous eval runs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if prior eval cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) did not fully release VM resources, slots may be permanently occupied until manual intervention.

Lower confidence — eval runner token or org-resolution failure upstream of createAgent: run-status-probes.mjs line 1882 skips if args.token is absent, but the check status is 'fail' not 'skip', and the scheduler error is explicit, so this is unlikely to be the primary cause.

Monitor the remote-agents feature status after remediation; features.json sets degradedAfterFailures=1, so a single passing run of remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state will restore the feature to healthy.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-eligible nodes shows available (unallocated) vm slots at the time of the eval run, the capacity-exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling or admission error would need to be investigated.

If the pod spec's node affinity/selector is found to be misconfigured such that zero nodes are actually eligible (not just 2), the root cause would shift to a configuration error rather than capacity exhaustion.

If the eval runner logs show the check was skipped due to a missing token (run-status-probes.mjs line 1882) rather than reaching the scheduler, the infrastructure capacity hypothesis would be disproved.
If a subsequent re-run of the eval immediately succeeds without any cluster changes, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief spike in concurrent VM usage) rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.

If the 4 non-matching nodes are found to have been recently tainted or labeled in a way that removed them from eligibility, the root cause would be a node configuration change rather than VM quota exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested counts on all eligible nodes before attempting agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct pre-condition failure rather than a scheduler timeout.
Add a VM slot leak detection eval that periodically audits running peer-pod VMs against known active eval sessions and flags any orphaned VMs that should have been cleaned up.
Add a node eligibility eval that verifies the expected number of nodes match the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector, catching configuration drift before it causes scheduling failures.

Consider adding a latency-bucketed eval that distinguishes between 'pod scheduled but agent slow to ready' (a runtime issue) and 'pod never scheduled' (a capacity or affinity issue), to improve signal specificity in future failures.

Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, or remote-agent-runtime that returns a scheduled pod and non-empty evidence would indicate the failure was transient capacity exhaustion rather than a persistent resource deficit.

Cluster node inspection showing kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are available and not exhausted on the two affinity-matching nodes would suggest the pod's node affinity/selector rules are misconfigured rather than capacity being the bottleneck.

followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on eligible nodes before attempting agent creation, and fails fast with a capacity-specific message if slots are at or near zero.
Add a persistent-pod audit eval that detects leaked or long-running remote-agent pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots beyond a configurable TTL, alerting before capacity is fully exhausted.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector meets a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 2 nodes with available vm slots), catching pool shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.

Add a sibling-correlation eval that automatically flags when all checks under a feature fail with the same scheduler message within the same run window, distinguishing infrastructure-layer failures from application-layer regressions earlier.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected because agent creation never completed — the pod remained unscheduled for 144 seconds before the eval timed out.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state) confirms that no schedulable node exists for the peer-pod VM at the time of the eval run. Because the agent pod never started, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never returned an agent, and all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) remained absent, causing the contract validation to fail completely. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or a prior eval run that did not clean up peer-pod VMs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new agent pods.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, meaning the effective schedulable pool is already small and any VM saturation on those 2 nodes causes a total scheduling failure.

TERTIARY — peer-pod VM leak from a previous eval run: if withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) did not successfully release a VM from an earlier run, the leaked VM would hold a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot and reduce available capacity.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — cluster node count insufficient for the expected remote-agent workload: the 6-node cluster with only 2 kata-capable nodes may be undersized for concurrent eval and production scheduling demand.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent evals (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod the eval runner attempted to schedule was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence of a passing run exists in history, and zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were returned, confirming the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource capacity on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) indicates that no schedulable node exists for a new peer-pod VM. Because the pod never started, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completed, leaving all four required evidence fields unpopulated and causing the expected-output contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256) to fail entirely. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' and '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' across 0/6 nodes, with preemption also unavailable.
failed-check.timing: check failed at latencyMs=127112, well before the outageLatencyMs threshold of 360000, meaning the pod was stuck unscheduled for 120s before the eval timed out.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the agent process never starting.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error, pod stuck for 144s, zero evidence keys returned.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod stuck for 144s, zero evidence keys returned.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; if the pod cannot be scheduled this call never resolves successfully, so no evidence is written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never starts.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:179-187: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are both marked required=true; degradedAfterFailures=1 means the feature is in a degraded state after this single run.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource quota exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: existing peer-pod VMs from prior runs or other workloads have consumed all available slots, leaving no capacity for new agent pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity/selector rules, meaning only 2 nodes are ever eligible. If those 2 nodes have even a small vm quota, any concurrent load exhausts it. Supported by '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' in failed-check.message.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie peer-pod VMs from previous eval runs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if prior eval cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) did not fully release VM resources, slots may be permanently occupied until manual intervention.

Lower confidence — eval runner token or org-resolution failure upstream of createAgent: run-status-probes.mjs line 1882 skips if args.token is absent, but the check status is 'fail' not 'skip', and the scheduler error is explicit, so this is unlikely to be the primary cause.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-eligible nodes shows available (unallocated) vm slots at the time of the eval run, the capacity-exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling or admission error would need to be investigated.

If the pod spec's node affinity/selector is found to be misconfigured such that zero nodes are actually eligible (not just 2), the root cause would shift to a configuration error rather than capacity exhaustion.

If the eval runner logs show the check was skipped due to a missing token (run-status-probes.mjs line 1882) rather than reaching the scheduler, the infrastructure capacity hypothesis would be disproved.
If a subsequent re-run of the eval immediately succeeds without any cluster changes, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief spike in concurrent VM usage) rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.

If the 4 non-matching nodes are found to have been recently tainted or labeled in a way that removed them from eligibility, the root cause would be a node configuration change rather than VM quota exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested counts on all eligible nodes before attempting agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct pre-condition failure rather than a scheduler timeout.
Add a VM slot leak detection eval that periodically audits running peer-pod VMs against known active eval sessions and flags any orphaned VMs that should have been cleaned up.
Add a node eligibility eval that verifies the expected number of nodes match the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector, catching configuration drift before it causes scheduling failures.

Consider adding a latency-bucketed eval that distinguishes between 'pod scheduled but agent slow to ready' (a runtime issue) and 'pod never scheduled' (a capacity or affinity issue), to improve signal specificity in future failures.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected because agent creation never completed — the pod remained unscheduled for 144 seconds before the eval timed out.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state) confirms that no schedulable node exists for the peer-pod VM at the time of the eval run. Because the agent pod never started, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never returned an agent, and all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) remained absent, causing the contract validation to fail completely. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler error 'pod stuck unscheduled for 144s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod’s node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
sibling.remote-agent-create: identical scheduler error (120s unscheduled), confirming the capacity problem predates the runtime check and is not isolated to one eval.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error (144s unscheduled), confirming all three remote-agent checks hit the same constraint.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, model, provider, or message was ever collected, consistent with pod never starting.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent, confirming the agent creation step was the earliest failure point.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918 — this call would block on pod scheduling and never return a usable agent under current cluster conditions.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=148575, endedAt=2026-07-02T21:40:35.839Z — the eval ran to its near-timeout boundary waiting for the pod, consistent with a scheduling deadlock rather than a fast API error.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or a prior eval run that did not clean up peer-pod VMs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new agent pods.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, meaning the effective schedulable pool is already small and any VM saturation on those 2 nodes causes a total scheduling failure.

TERTIARY — peer-pod VM leak from a previous eval run: if withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) did not successfully release a VM from an earlier run, the leaked VM would hold a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot and reduce available capacity.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — cluster node count insufficient for the expected remote-agent workload: the 6-node cluster with only 2 kata-capable nodes may be undersized for concurrent eval and production scheduling demand.

reproductionSteps.label: Run only the remote-agent-runtime eval probe against production-api
reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow to reproduce the scheduling failure.

reproductionSteps.label: Run all three remote-agent checks together to confirm shared scheduling failure
reproductionSteps.details: Confirms whether the capacity problem affects the full feature or only one check.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on the 2 eligible nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Replace <kata-peerpods-node-selector> with the actual label used by the node affinity rule in the agent pod spec. This will show current allocatable vs. requested VM slots.

reproductionSteps.label: List all running or pending pods that hold kata.peerpods.io/vm resources to identify leaks
reproductionSteps.command: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide | grep -i peer
reproductionSteps.details: Look for pods in Running or Pending state that may be holding VM slots from prior eval runs that did not clean up.

reproductionSteps.label: Check for stuck or leaked peer-pod VMs from prior eval runs
reproductionSteps.details: Review whether withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs successfully terminated agent pods from the previous eval cycle. A leaked VM would reduce available capacity for subsequent runs.

affectedAreas.label: Kubernetes kata peer-pods VM scheduling layer (production-api cluster)
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on the 2 eligible nodes, making this the earliest and most direct failure boundary (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature — all three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature (lines 183-185) failed with the same scheduler error, indicating the entire feature's eval surface is blocked by the capacity constraint.
affectedAreas.details: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false. With degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2, two required check failures meet the outage threshold in the feature registry.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — createAgent call for remote agent type
affectedAreas.reason: The runner branch at line 1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote', which triggers peer-pod VM scheduling. This is the code path that blocks and ultimately times out (source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918).
affectedAreas.details: The withCleanup wrapper at line 1916 is also implicated if prior runs did not release VM slots.

affectedAreas.label: Expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime
affectedAreas.reason: All 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) and the message assertion ('hello from aura') are unverifiable because the agent never started (source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:262-270, expected-output.missing-required-evidence).

recommendedNextActions: Immediately inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm resource usage on the 2 eligible nodes to determine whether slots are currently exhausted or have recovered since the eval run at 2026-07-02T21:40:35Z.
Audit running and pending pods across all namespaces for leaked peer-pod VMs from prior eval or production runs; terminate any that are no longer needed to free VM slots.

Review the withCleanup logic in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1916) to confirm it reliably releases peer-pod VM resources even when the eval probe fails mid-execution (e.g., on timeout or exception).

Assess whether the 2-node kata-capable pool is sized appropriately for concurrent eval and production remote-agent demand; consider adding more kata-capable nodes or increasing the kata.peerpods.io/vm limit per node if the pool is undersized.

Verify the node affinity/selector configuration for remote-agent pods to confirm the 4 non-matching nodes are intentionally excluded and that no labeling drift has reduced the schedulable pool below its intended size.
Re-run the three remote-agent eval checks after any remediation to confirm all 5 required evidence fields are returned and the 'hello from aura' assertion passes.

Note: this is an eval-observed failure. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; do not escalate as a confirmed user-facing outage until cluster inspection or a passing eval run provides additional signal.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run the remote-agent-runtime eval probe in isolation
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the scheduling failure is still present or was transient. A pass would return all 5 required evidence fields and satisfy the 'hello from aura' assertion (expected-output.contract).

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on eligible nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly measures whether VM slots are exhausted on the 2 schedulable nodes, confirming or ruling out the capacity exhaustion hypothesis (failed-check.message).

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List all pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm resources across namespaces
recommendedVerifierProbes.command: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.containers[].resources.requests["kata.peerpods.io/vm"] != null) | {name: .metadata.name, namespace: .metadata.namespace, phase: .status.phase}'
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies any leaked or stuck peer-pod VMs from prior eval runs that may be holding capacity (possible cause: VM leak from withCleanup failure in run-status-probes.mjs line 1916).

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Check node affinity and selector on the remote-agent pod spec
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the 4 non-matching nodes are excluded by design (correct label) or by a misconfiguration, and whether the 2 eligible nodes are the intended and only schedulable targets (failed-check.message: '4 node(s) didn’t match Pod’s node affinity/selector').

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agent sibling checks together to confirm shared failure scope
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Verifies that all three checks fail or pass together, confirming the shared scheduling dependency (sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the 2 kata-capable nodes shows available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity at the time of the eval run, the scheduling failure would need a different explanation (e.g., a misconfigured node selector or resource request in the pod spec).

If a subsequent eval run with no other concurrent workloads succeeds and returns all 5 required evidence fields, the failure was transient capacity contention rather than a persistent exhaustion or leak.
If the node affinity/selector on the agent pod spec was recently changed to exclude the 2 kata-capable nodes, the root cause would be a configuration regression rather than VM capacity exhaustion.
If the 4 non-matching nodes are found to have kata.peerpods.io/vm resources but a different label mismatch, the problem would be a node labeling or affinity misconfiguration rather than capacity.

If no peer-pod VMs are found running or leaked in the cluster at the time of investigation, the root cause may be that the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit per node is set too low relative to demand.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct 'warn' status rather than a scheduling timeout.

Add a VM-leak detection eval that lists all peer-pod VMs older than a configurable threshold (e.g., 10 minutes) and fails if any are found, catching cleanup failures before they exhaust capacity for subsequent runs.

Add a node-pool health eval that verifies the expected number of kata-capable nodes are Ready and carry the required node labels/taints, alerting on pool shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.

Consider a latency-banded eval for remote-agent-create that warns at a lower threshold (e.g., 60s) when pod scheduling is slow, providing earlier signal before the full 120-144s unschedulable timeout is reached.
